clue.text: Matters of principle? One switches sides, baring teeth

indicators.note: the letters standing for the two sides, left and right, trade places in the word

parts.note: morals are matters of principle

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their principles by changing allegiance and shows their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One switches sides' means L (left) and R (right) swap places in MORALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Molars are the grinding back teeth, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: A number of balls to 'ang in the air

definitions.meaning: in cricket an ... is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ang' tells you to drop the H from the second sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over is a fixed number of deliveries; the second sense is a dropped-aitch hover.

clue.text: Look pale and cold, having plunged into the drink for a stint

indicators.note: the first pieces dive inside the drink, so they sit within it

parts.note: ale is a drink
lo is an old word for look
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Someone goes pale and cold after jumping into the water for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun stint means a limited allowance or allotted share, the older sense of the word.

clue.text: Governing body had nurse brought before it

indicators.note: the nurse is placed in front of the word for had, so it comes first

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
ate means had, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: A board is told it has had a nurse summoned before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative or governing council, as in Rome or a university.

clue.text: Short journey to social event? One's relieved when it's good!

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter of the word for journey goes

parts.note: a ride is a journey
a dance is a social event

explanation.surface: A brief trip to a party leaves someone relieved if it goes well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'good riddance', said with relief when something unwanted goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is getting rid of something, and 'good riddance' is the cry of relief.

clue.text: Various earlier CDs I borrow — last two not in places where they should be

indicators.note: various suggests the letters arranged in different ways
the final two letters of the word borrow are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone borrowing older CDs finds they are not shelved where they belong.
explanation.walkthrough: BORR (borrow without OW) joins EARLIER, CDS and I as fodder for 'Various'.
explanation.definitionFit: Record libraries lend discs, so they are the proper home for borrowed CDs.

clue.text: Very loud cry for advance? The reverse when one's retreated

indicators.note: the reverse tells you to read the combined pieces backwards

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
onward is a cry urging people forward

explanation.surface: A loud shout to charge is followed by the opposite when troops pull back.
explanation.walkthrough: FF + ONWARD read backwards gives the answer; 'when one's' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops drawn off have been withdrawn or pulled back, so it fits retreated.

clue.text: Down with Henry! Shame!

parts.note: a bas is French for down with
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A protester shouts against a king named Henry, calling it a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bas' (French 'down with') is a protest cry, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone ashamed or embarrassed, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Beauty arrives having hidden wrinkles

indicators.note: the word for arrives conceals the next piece inside itself

parts.note: comes means arrives
lines are wrinkles

explanation.surface: A beauty turns up having concealed her wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Comeliness is attractiveness or good looks, a synonym of beauty.

clue.text: Greek girl embraced by this Roman

indicators.note: the girl is held inside the Latin word, so it goes within

parts.note: hic is Latin, the Romans' language, for this
Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Greek girl is hugged by a Roman man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenic means relating to Greece or the Greeks, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Panics finding a gangster with guns?

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous gangster
arms are guns

explanation.surface: People take fright on seeing a mobster carrying weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms as a plural noun are sudden frights or panics.

clue.text: Where a lot may re-gather to drink gin, possibly

definitions.text: Where a lot may re-gather to drink gin, possibly

indicators.note: re-gather means the letters are collected again in another order
possibly adds that the letters could be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crowd meets again to enjoy a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WHERE A LOT and GIN are rearranged, and the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is a bar or pub where people gather for drinks, a jocular idiom.

clue.text: Dressing up in robes, I annoy a Methodist

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in signals that the letters are concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone dresses in robes, irritating a Methodist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a salad dressing made of egg and oil.

clue.text: Bristle on Dad's face — time to shave it off?

indicators.note: on means placed after the preceding letter in an across answer
the face of a word is its front, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: an awn is a bristle on a grass head

explanation.surface: A father's stubble prompts a morning shave.
explanation.walkthrough: Daybreak is the time a man might shave off the bristle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the early morning, a typical time for shaving.

clue.text: Abandoned a financial career for an academic position in Paris

parts.note: left means abandoned
banking is a financial career, shortened to bank

explanation.surface: Someone quits finance to take a university job in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Left Bank of the Seine is home to the Sorbonne and the Latin Quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the Parisian district of universities and scholars.

clue.text: Drunk disposing of litre, male wanting drink for good health!

indicators.note: disposing of means removing the letter for litre

parts.note: blotto is slang for drunk
to sup is to drink, and a sup is a drink

explanation.surface: A drunk man wanting another drink toasts everyone's health.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOTTO less L gives BOTTO; 'wanting' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a drinking toast, like cheers or here's to your health.

clue.text: Brown mineral extractable from mine with toil

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brown ore can be got out of a mine with hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Limonite is a brownish iron ore mineral.

clue.text: A wing? It could make flier, first and last, mobile

indicators.note: could make suggests building something new from the letters
first and last means just the outside letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A wing might let a bird become a mobile flier.
explanation.walkthrough: FR (the ends of 'flier') plus MOBILE is rearranged; 'mobile' looks like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's wing is its front limb, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Hairy growth he removed from the wood

indicators.note: the letters for he are taken out of what follows

parts.note: taken as written
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A hairy plant growth is cut away from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: THE + ASH with HE removed leaves the answer, British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Tash is informal British for a moustache, a growth of hair.

clue.text: Miniskirt enthusiast, one gathered, is attractive but not modern

indicators.note: gathered means the designer's name collects the letter inside

parts.note: Mary Quant was the designer who popularised the miniskirt
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fan of short skirts gathers material for an old-fashioned look.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the 1960s British fashion designer behind the miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means charmingly old-fashioned, appealing but dated.

clue.text: Famous Neapolitan or Corsican involved with EU

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled together and reordered

explanation.surface: A celebrated Neapolitan or Corsican is caught up with European affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the renowned tenor born in Naples.

clue.text: I love going round church — right medium to bring the divine alive?

definitions.text: medium to bring the divine alive?

indicators.note: going round means the first pieces surround the word for church

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A believer circles a church seeking a way to make God present.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth ichor is the fluid flowing in gods' veins, their blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor was the ethereal fluid in the veins of the gods, keeping them alive.

clue.text: Odd bits of culture that you see here

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Scattered fragments of culture are on show here.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the very thing being read: a crossword puzzle hint.
explanation.definitionFit: What a solver sees here is a crossword hint, so it refers to itself.

clue.text: This troubled rabbi completely losing heart for a time in Israel

indicators.note: troubled means the letters are disturbed and reordered
all the middle letters go, leaving just the outside ones

explanation.surface: An anxious rabbi loses his nerve during a period in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: TISH comes from rearranging THIS, then RI is rabbi without its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tishri is a month of the Jewish calendar, the first of the civil year.

clue.text: Regardless of other things, is mischief maker taking fool in?

indicators.note: taking with in means the fool is drawn inside
in completes the phrase taking in, meaning holding inside

parts.note: taken as written
a nit is a fool
an elf is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A trickster takes in a fool regardless of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' and 'in' together say the fool is held inside; 'mischief maker' tempts you towards IMP, which does not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: In itself means considered alone, apart from other factors.

clue.text: Dry aristocrat entertained by tragic female

indicators.note: the aristocrat is a guest within the female's name

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's tragic heroine
an earl is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A tragic heroine hosts a nobleman without shedding a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearless means dry-eyed, without crying.

clue.text: Row about 2p — should one have offered more?

indicators.note: about means the row goes around the coins

parts.note: a tier is a row
two pence is written PP, two p's

explanation.surface: An argument about a 2p coin asks whether more should have been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like an argument but is a tier; a tipper leaving 2p is mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper is one who leaves a gratuity, perhaps too small.
